author: Mark Atwood
text:
Coordinated workspace-wide API break — needs explicit owner approval.

The fix is straightforward (return Result<bool, Self::Error> from task_list_has_tasks and propagate Err to serverFail in handler), but per the bead body the same shape is present in three crates:
  - jmap-tasks-server::TasksBackend::task_list_has_tasks
  - jmap-calendars-server::CalendarsBackend::calendar_has_events
  - jmap-contacts-server::ContactsBackend::address_book_has_contents

Per the workspace canonical-template propagation rule, the right action is a single coordinated commit changing all three. The bead body says: 'the maintainer should decide whether to do the workspace-wide sweep in one pass.'

Recommendation: option (a) do the coordinated sweep in a single commit across tasks/calendars/contacts. Rationale: the breaking-change cost is the same whether it lands as one commit or three; doing it as one keeps the call-site shape uniform across the workspace and avoids a multi-week period where calendars and contacts are still on the bare-bool shape while tasks has moved. The crates are all pre-publish; cost to external consumers is zero today.

Alternative: option (b) tasks-server-local fix now + follow-up sweep bead for calendars/contacts. This was the path taken for JMAP-h47t.22 (auth-contract rustdoc) and JMAP-h47t.24 (BackendSetError catchall). Both are arguably the wrong precedent — they're docs-only or behavior-preserving — whereas this is a trait-signature break that benefits from atomic application.

Escalating because (a) is a coordinated multi-crate API break and (b) the bead body itself explicitly defers the scope decision to the maintainer.
